notes.content: Thank you for your interest in Sacramento State! This articulation agreement displays the lower-division courses required in the major: Sacramento State courses on the left and approved (articulated) transfer courses on the right. Any upper-division coursework included in this agreement will receive lower-division subject credit only. Students are advised to complete the lower-division coursework in this agreement prior to transfer. Additional Resources: See the University Catalog for the full listing of degree requirements for this major. Visit our Sac State Apply page for more information about our campus! Visit the Admissions website for current transfer admission requirements. Connect with an Admissions Counselor . Questions about this agreement? Contact: Kristen Anderegg, Liberal Studies Lead Advisor at: kristena@csus.edu

notes.content: Students must earn a minimum grade of "C-" or higher in all courses required in the major. A minimum 2.00 GPA is required in each area. To enter a California credential program, a minimum GPA of 2.67 is required by the time of application to a California teaching credential program. Students are encouraged not to petition for CR/NR or P/NP grading option in Liberal Studies courses taken at the community college. In addition to the admission requirements for the university, transfer students are strongly encouraged to complete the majority of the courses listed in this articulation agreement including upper-division course options when possible and foreign language, if necessary. The more requirements completed prior to transfer translates to fewer requirements to complete after transfer. Please visit the Liberal Studies website for additional information on course substitutions and options for upper-division courses not listed on this agreement. The Liberal Studies Program satisfies Sacramento State General Education requirements. Students intending to transfer as Liberal Studies majors should follow the Liberal Studies articulation agreement for their community college. Consult with a Liberal Studies advisor for the possibility of course substitutions for previously completed coursework or for courses that are not articulated. Only a Liberal Studies advisor is authorized to provide substitutions for the courses in the agreement below. Students with catalog rights Fall 2025 or later should complete a course that satisfies CSU GE Area 6 (Ethnic Studies). Cal-GETC Area 6 (Ethnic Studies) courses also satisfy this requirement. For the most current major information, visit the Liberal Studies website .
notes.contentHtml:
1. Students must earn a minimum grade of "C-" or higher in all courses required in the major. A minimum 2.00 GPA is required in each area. To enter a California credential program, a minimum GPA of 2.67 is required by the time of application to a California teaching credential program. Students are encouraged not to petition for CR/NR or P/NP grading option in Liberal Studies courses taken at the community college.
  2. In addition to the admission requirements for the university, transfer students are strongly encouraged to complete the majority of the courses listed in this articulation agreement including upper-division course options when possible and foreign language, if necessary. The more requirements completed prior to transfer translates to fewer requirements to complete after transfer. Please visit the Liberal Studies website for additional information on course substitutions and options for upper-division courses not listed on this agreement.
  3. The Liberal Studies Program satisfies Sacramento State General Education requirements. Students intending to transfer as Liberal Studies majors should follow the Liberal Studies articulation agreement for their community college. Consult with a Liberal Studies advisor for the possibility of course substitutions for previously completed coursework or for courses that are not articulated. Only a Liberal Studies advisor is authorized to provide substitutions for the courses in the agreement below.
  4. Students with catalog rights Fall 2025 or later should complete a course that satisfies CSU GE Area 6 (Ethnic Studies). Cal-GETC Area 6 (Ethnic Studies) courses also satisfy this requirement.
  5. For the most current major information, visit the Liberal Studies website.
